question:
Bind the executed-transition record to the machine results it stores. Today reference/python/cap/execution_record.py validate_execution_record(record, base_dir, repo_dir) checks that every referenced file exists, that every execution.inputs[].sha256 matches its file, that every revision resolves, and criterion coverage; it never reads a stored result and never compares the record's claims with it (run 007 reproduced the accepted contradictions: validation_artifacts/ameba_cycle/run_007_record_binding_gap/).

Environment: the current working directory is the repository root. The validator lives in reference/python/cap/execution_record.py, returns a list of problem strings and never raises on a bad record; _revision_exists already shells out to git. Its tests are reference/python/tests/test_execution_record_validator.py (fixture: examples/transition_execution_record_example.json, whose stand-in files are examples/transition_execution_record/check_result_c1.txt and examples/transition_execution_record/executor_receipt.json). Stored check results in this repository are text files that end with one line 'exit=<int>' (see validation_artifacts/ameba_cycle/run_006_com_log_link/checks/). Receipts are what the NoMCP router writes (see validation_artifacts/ameba_cycle/run_006_com_log_link/nomcp_coding_receipt.json): top-level 'decision' and 'fallback_used'; 'first_attempt' and, when used, 'fallback_attempt', each with 'model_served'; 'inputs' with 'packet': {'sha256': ...} and 'check_files': [{'sha256': ...}, ...]. Tests run with python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider <files> after sys.path.insert(0, <reference/python>).

Required changes, with exactly these rules, each producing one problem string that names the record path and the offending value; keep every existing check and problem string unchanged and add the new rules after the existing coverage rules:
1. exit line: for every checks[i] whose result_ref resolves, the stored file must contain exactly one line matching ^exit=(-?\d+)$ and its integer must equal checks[i].exit_code; problems 'checks[i].result_ref: no single exit= line in <ref>' and 'checks[i].exit_code: recorded <n>, stored result says <m>'.
2. command: checks[i].command must equal the check_command of the criterion named by checks[i].criterion_id (string equality of the command text); problem 'checks[i].command: differs from criterion <id> check_command'.
3. revision, applied only when repo_dir is given: resolve object.revision_after, observation_after.revision_after and every checks[i].revision_checked with git -C <repo_dir> rev-parse --verify <rev>^{commit}; a short and a full SHA of one commit are the same object. Every resolved checks[i].revision_checked must equal the resolved observation_after.revision_after, and that must equal the resolved object.revision_after; problems 'checks[i].revision_checked: <rev> is not the re-observed revision <observed>' and 'observation_after.revision_after: <rev> is not object.revision_after <rev>'. Revisions that do not resolve are already reported by the existing rule and are skipped here.
4. receipt fields, applied when verdict.provenance_established is true and execution.receipt_ref resolves: the file must parse as a JSON object, else 'execution.receipt_ref: not a JSON object: <ref>'. Then compare VALUES IN THESE FIELDS ONLY: (a) the receipt's top-level 'decision' must equal execution.decision, else 'execution.receipt_ref: decision <record> is not the receipt decision <receipt>'; (b) the served model of the closing attempt, i.e. receipt['fallback_attempt']['model_served'] when receipt['fallback_used'] is true and receipt['first_attempt']['model_served'] otherwise, must equal execution.actor.model_served, else 'execution.receipt_ref: model_served <record> is not the receipt served model <receipt>'; (c) every execution.inputs[].sha256 must be among the set of receipt['inputs']['packet']['sha256'] and receipt['inputs']['check_files'][*]['sha256'], else 'execution.receipt_ref: input <sha256> is not among the receipt inputs'. A field that is absent or of the wrong type yields 'execution.receipt_ref: receipt lacks <field path>'. Text found anywhere else in the receipt (notes, answers, check output) counts for nothing.
Extend the module docstring by one paragraph naming the four rules and stating what a passing record now means: the named links between the record and its stored carriers are checked; full provenance of the execution is not established by this.
5. examples: append the line 'exit=0' to examples/transition_execution_record/check_result_c1.txt (keep the pytest output above it) and rewrite examples/transition_execution_record/executor_receipt.json into the router's shape with the same values: {"run_id": "run_example_transition_001", "decision": "apply_candidate", "fallback_used": false, "first_attempt": {"model_requested": "example-model-requested", "model_served": "example-model-served"}, "inputs": {"packet": {"sha256": "76f0fdbab02bcc165e233664c37f5400510461a2dd6bb821f443f76335f6a0b5"}, "check_files": []}} so the shipped example resolves with and without --repo.
6. tests in reference/python/tests/test_execution_record_validator.py: keep every existing test unchanged; add one test per rule (a stored result with exit=1 under a check that says pass and exit_code 0; a command that differs from the criterion; a check at e65b9af4 while the record re-observed another revision; a stray text file as receipt with provenance_established true; a router-shaped receipt whose decision, served model and packet sha256 differ from the record while the record's values appear in its 'notes'), plus two positive tests: a short SHA of the re-observed commit as revision_checked resolves without problems, and a router-shaped receipt whose fields match resolves without problems, plus the example itself still resolving with repo_dir.
